description: Klatt 1980 formant BANDWIDTHS (Hz). Bandwidth sets how sharply a formant rings; radius = exp(-pi*BW/SR) (tools/corner_words.r_from_bw). Companion to klatt_1980_formants.json (center freqs) and vowel_formants.json (Peterson-Barney). Captured from the project NotebookLM (Klatt 1980, Table I/II/III) 2026-05-29.
source: Dennis H. Klatt, 'Software for a cascade/parallel formant synthesizer', JASA 67(3):971-995, 1980.
notes: Klatt vowels are ALL-POLE (R1-R5 cascade, no zeros). The only explicit antiresonance is NASAL (RNP/RNZ). Fricatives use parallel-branch amplitudes, not zeros. Higher formants use constant default bandwidths.

default_high_formant_bw.comment: Table I; B4/B5 held constant across vowels, F4/F5 ~3300/3850

nasal_pole_zero.comment: Table I; nasal pole fixed at 270 Hz. Non-nasal: FNZ=270 cancels it. Nasalized vowel: shift F1 up ~100 Hz, set FNZ = mean(F1+100, 270) -> pole-zero-pole split that reduces F1 amplitude.

vowels._comment: Table II isolated-vowel bandwidths. NotebookLM quoted the three corner vowels /i a u/ verbatim; the rest of Table II can be added when needed. Map: i=ee, a=ah, u=oo.

nasal_murmurs._comment: Table III. Higher-frequency nasal character simulated by WIDENING bandwidths (B2/B3), not by extra poles/zeros.
